findings.body: `missing` means only “no nonblank SAP name was resolved,” not “no SAP lines exist.” Consequently, a matched or actual-only code whose scoped transactions have null/blank `acct_name` enters the outline fallback and displays an MIS label, although the specification reserves that fallback for codes with no SAP lines and requires an otherwise unnamed code to remain bare. The bare-code test does not catch this because it supplies an outline for a different GL code. Preserve whether any scoped SAP row exists and apply the outline only when that count is zero.
findings.title: Not done: only budget-only codes use the MIS fallback

findings.body: The complete list exists only in `aria-label` on a plain `<span>`. A span maps to the generic role, for which author-provided accessible names are prohibited/ignored by accessibility APIs; while collapsed, the list itself is absent and the button announces only “n more account names.” Testing Library's `findByLabelText` merely finds the attribute and does not verify the browser accessibility tree. Put the full text in screen-reader-visible content or name an element whose role supports naming.
findings.title: Not done: the row’s accessible name includes the full name list

findings.body: The supplied check explicitly stops at fixture answers through the component boundary. Here the Ask API is mocked with already-resolved `rowLabels`, and the statement fixture likewise injects its finished label, so the check never exercises SAP-name selection, effective plant scope, budget-only detection, pinned-outline lookup, or snapshot persistence—the covered behavior a client depends on. It therefore skips material parts of both Done-when items and would not expose the incorrect unnamed-actual fallback above.
findings.title: Not done: functional check

findings.body: The query caps raw `acct_name` spellings at `MAX_ROWS` (1000 by default) before whitespace/case normalization and group counting. If a GL has more raw spellings, variants outside the first 1000 are silently omitted; a normalized group spread across those variants can therefore lose counts, become the wrong primary name, or produce the wrong “+n more” list. Normalize/aggregate in SQL before the cap, or page all raw groups before ranking.
findings.title: Normalize all scoped spellings before applying the row cap

findings.body: All added label tests stop at a fake warehouse, fake outline repository, fake conversation transaction, or mocked frontend API response. The required running-API/real-database/browser proof for Done-when items 1 and 2 therefore does not exist. Because this branch intentionally cannot emit `rowLabels` until GL-ANSWER-WIRING integrates the resolver into `ChatService`, that task should add the end-to-end proof instead of treating these component tests as the final user-path coverage.
findings.title: Later: prove labels through the running Ask stack → GL-ANSWER-WIRING
